subject: [Incident] Nebula-lite-2b elevated errors & recovery plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@nebula.ai>, ops@nebula.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Incident] Nebula-lite-2b elevated 5xx/timeouts — notice & immediate mitigation

Hi Susan / Nebula ops team,

Quick heads up: we detected a spike in 5xx responses and generation timeouts originating from requests routed to nebula-lite-2b starting ~07:50 PT. Symptoms: increased 500/504 rates for long-sequence generations (tokens > 2k), intermittent stalled streams, and a small subset of requests returning truncated outputs.

Impact: approximately 6–12% of traffic to nebula-lite-2b for your account failed between 07:50–08:35 PT. We estimate this affected ~430 requests for Nebula Analytics (we pulled request IDs and sample traces).

Immediate actions we took:
- Automated routing rule applied at 07:58 PT to steer Nebula Analytics traffic away from nebula-lite-2b to nebula-stable-2b (compatible generation quality).
- Scaled the nebula-lite pool by +2 nodes and disabled an experimental memory-eviction optimization.
- Enabled detailed debug logging and captured KV/cache traces.

Next updates: internal triage in progress; ETA for customer-facing follow-up is ~1–2 hours. We will provide a recovery update and a short timeline of events.

Attachments: grafana-nebula-lite-errspike.png (panel), nebula-lite-error-trace.log (sample traces)

We sincerely apologize for the disruption — we know this impacts your runs. If you prefer we keep routing all Nebula Analytics traffic to nebula-stable-2b for the rest of the day, let me know and we’ll make that change immediately.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: [Incident] Nebula-lite-2b elevated 5xx/timeouts — notice & immediate mitigation

Ben — looping in triage notes.

On Mon, Nov 9, 2026 at 08:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick heads up: we detected a spike in 5xx responses and generation timeouts originating from requests routed to nebula-lite-2b starting ~07:50 PT.

Triage summary (so far):
- Initial signal shows memory pressure on nebula-lite-2b hosts when sequence length > ~1800 tokens after an internal kernel upgrade pushed yesterday (kernel v3.2.1-opt).
- The new eviction heuristic occasionally purges active KV entries under certain shuffle patterns, causing repeated cold fetches and backlog at the RT emulator — leads to stalled token generation and 504s.
- Engineering reverted the kernel change at 08:22 PT; we also triggered a rolling restart of the nebula-lite pool and applied a temporary routing rule (Ben’s note).

Actions in flight:
- Priyom: collecting heapdumps and KV cache snapshots (links below).
- Ops: will keep nebula-stable routing in place for Nebula Analytics until Thursday EOD or until explicit confirmation from customer.
- SRE: create alert for >3% 5xx across model pool for sequence length buckets >1500.

Runbook link: incident-runbook-link.txt (internal).
Attached: rtc-trace-sample.json (pushed to incident folder), short grafana snapshot.

Marissa Cole
Engineering Lead, Model Reliability
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Susan Liu <susan.liu@nebula.ai>, ops@nebula.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [Incident] Nebula-lite-2b elevated 5xx/timeouts — recovery and next steps

Susan — thanks for your patience. Final update for the day:

Status: Recovered. Traffic to nebula-lite-2b for your account returned to baseline error rates at 17:10 PT after the rollback and rolling restarts. We left the traffic steering in place while monitoring and made no changes to your production routing without your sign-off.

Root cause (summary): A recently deployed kernel optimization (v3.2.1-opt) changed the KV eviction ordering for certain multi-turn workloads. Under heavy long-sequence patterns this caused high cache churn and increased backend fetch latency; that backend latency propagated back into the generation runtime and produced 500/504 responses for in-flight requests.

Remediations completed today:
- Reverted kernel change (08:22 PT) and rolled back the eviction heuristic.
- Added sequence-length-aware circuit breaker and tightened SLOs on backend fetch latency.
- New alerting for >2% 5xx by sequence-length bucket.
- Scheduled a controlled A/B test of a tuned eviction policy next week behind canary routing.

Customer-facing commitments:
- We will publish a single-page postmortem draft by 11/11 with full timeline, affected request IDs, and concrete actions. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-incident-nebula-lite-2b
- We will credit Nebula Analytics for any failed generation token charges during 07:50–08:35 PT (HS-49823).
- Offer: If you prefer, we can continue to route Nebula Analytics to nebula-stable-2b until Friday 11/13 — please confirm.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-nebula-lite-2b.docx (internal draft)

Thanks again; we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and coordinate any replays you want us to run.
